role: the maintainer three years from now
verdict: The spec does not yet meet this lens's definition of success: it plans its own staleness by keeping hand-written copies of facts that the product will generate (03's tables, 10 10.2's check prose, 05 5.2's Test cells) with nothing that compares the copy to the truth, and the same facts already live in two to four places, one of which (the merge ruleset) drifted inside round 8 itself; the largest gap is that there is no rule for how any stored file or any pinned external version evolves after v1.0.0.

findings.defect: The format tables of 03 are declared design input that the product generates elsewhere, so after v1 the spec holds a second, unmaintained copy of every format with no comparison to the generated reference.
findings.scenario: T021 lands rules.go and the generated docs/reference/project.md; a later PR adds a field to the spec type; generated passes because the reference regenerated; 03 3.2's table still lists the old field set; the next contributor reads 03, writes a spec with the old shape, and is refused by a validator the spec never described.
findings.change: Add to 03's opening: after the task that lands a format's generator, the spec page keeps only the intent, the annotated example and the rules that are design decisions, and replaces each field or rule table by a link to its generated reference page; tools/ci docs fails a spec page that contains a table whose header equals a generated table's header.
findings.cost: A sentence of policy, one docs rule, and a deletion pass on 03 after T021.

findings.defect: About 330 lines of 10 10.2 are check logic written in English, with pinned tool versions, runner labels and commit ids in prose (mise 2026.10.3, revive v1.17.0, testifylint v1.6.4, golangci-lint 2.14.0, cab976e, fsfe/reuse:6.2.0), while the code in tools/ci is the truth and nothing holds the two equal.
findings.scenario: mise.lock bumps golangci-lint; the lint row of 10 10.2 still describes the previous version's checkers and the revive internals; an agent asked to add a lint rule reads the row, implements against it, and the fixture test of ADR 0001 rule 14 fails for a reason the spec cannot explain; the PR body then quotes the stale row as evidence.
findings.change: Keep in 10 10.2 the step table, the grammar's rationale and the limits stated plainly; move the per-step detail (lint sub-rules, directive allowlist, hygiene list, forbidden-name matcher, the mise environment) to a generated docs/reference/ci.md written from tools/ci's own help and data, as 12 12.3 already does for commands; add a tools/ci docs rule that a version string or a 7 to 40 hex commit id in spec or ADR prose is a finding unless inside a code span that also names its source file.
findings.cost: One generator row, one docs rule, a rewrite of 10 10.2 to about a third of its length; the index's deferred row on the step table closes with it.

findings.defect: Every stored format has a version field and strict decoding, and only the manifest (N or N-1) and the event (ingest window) say what a reader does with another version; settings.yaml, render.json, toolchain.json, projects/<name>.json, memory entries and handoffs have no read-compatibility rule, and I16 forbids the rewrite a migration would be.
findings.scenario: romeu v1.3 adds a field to projects/<name>.json and bumps version to 2; a machine upgrades; the strict decoder refuses every version 1 record; run exits 2 on every project; someone writes a migration in a hurry that rewrites host state, which I16's scan then has to admit.
findings.change: Add one rule to 03's opening for every format: a reader at version N accepts N and N-1 and refuses older with a named error id; a new version is additive within a major; a major is a new ADR; where a file is rewritten whole by its owner (the project record, render.json) the owner writes the current version on its next write, and read-only consumers (romeu reading memory entries) never rewrite; name the one place migration code may live.
findings.cost: A policy paragraph, one error id, an ADR for the N/N-1 window as the product-wide rule, and a test per format in 10 10.1.

findings.defect: One idea has three spellings: apiVersion: romeu/v1 (spec, host settings), version: 1 as an integer (render, state, manifest, memory entry, handoff, catalog, run layout, probe result), and schema: runtime-event/v1 as a string (event, entry, view).
findings.scenario: A contributor adds the dora.v1 or a status schema and picks a fourth form; a generic reader that wants the version of any romeu file needs to know which family it belongs to first.
findings.change: Choose one form in 03's opening and apply it to every schema in 02 2.1's list; the schema check of tools/ci schema fails a schema without the field in that form.
findings.cost: A decision, a sentence, regenerated schemas and examples before T021.

findings.defect: The merge-ruleset fact changed (no review is required) and was patched into four places with the clause 'as measured on 2026-10-08' while the rule stays written beside its negation, and ADR 0001 rule 8 and ADR 0003 describe a code-owner review that does not exist because ADR 0008 chose not to rewrite them.
findings.scenario: An agent implementing T005 reads 12 12.4's merge row, which says 'one approving review, dismissed by a later push; code-owner review for ask-first paths' and, in the same cell, that the ruleset requires no review; it implements the approval line as if a reviewer will read it, and the PR body cites ADR 0001 rule 8 as the guarantee; three years on nobody can tell which sentence was true when.
findings.change: State the merge requirements once, in 05 5.4, as ADR 0008 decision 2 intends; 10 10.2 item a, 12 12.4 and 12 12.9 say only 'the merge requirements and what they are worth are in 05 5.4'; ADR 0001 rule 8 and ADR 0003 gain one Status line 'Superseded in part by ADR 0008 for the review requirement'; add that partial-supersede form to ADR 0001 rule 7 so sequences can check it.
findings.cost: Words in four sections, one new status form in rule 7, a sequences clause.

findings.defect: Five lists that two or more consumers must agree on are hand-written in two or three places each with no generator and no test: the dangerous git keys (05 5.1 -c list, I3 plant list, the doctor warn row, with three different memberships), the memory layout allowlist (I24, 08 8.1, memstore), the mise environment (04 4.3, 07 7.3, 07 7.4), the commands that ingest (04 4.2, 04 4.4, 13 13.4), and the reserved names (02 2.3 tree, 03 3.1 dir rule).
findings.scenario: A git CVE names a new config key; a PR adds it to gitsafe's -c list and to I3's plant; the doctor row is forgotten; doctor passes a host whose global config carries the key, and the review-checkout risk 5.4 describes is live and unreported.
findings.change: For each list name one home in the text and have the other places link to it without repeating the members; where two consumers are code (gitsafe and doctor; memstore and the spool reader; the ingest callers), add a 12 12.3 generator row so the second consumer is derived, and a test that the plant list of I3 equals the neutralized list of 05 5.1.
findings.cost: Words in ten places, three generator rows, two tests.

findings.defect: The vocabulary has 18 rows and a Not column that is empty in eleven, so the generated check enforces about seven phrases, while terms used on every page have no row (workload, manifest, event, entry, view, probe, journey, lesson, surface, module versus package) and product kits are called both kit and mixin (06 6.4 'Kind: mixin').
findings.scenario: A hundred agent PRs each pick kit or mixin, entry or event, module or package by local habit; error messages, help text and docs end with both names for each thing, and tools/ci vocabulary passes because the Not column never named the loser.
findings.change: Add a row per term above with a filled Not column (mixin -> kit; package versus module defined), and fill the Not column of the existing rows where a rival word exists (sandbox for generation, event for entry).
findings.cost: Fifteen table rows; the generated denylist grows with them.

findings.defect: The same person is 'operator' when the machine is meant (01 1.1, 05 5.4, 09 [O]) and 'maintainer' when the repository process is meant (05 5.3, 10 10.2, 12 12.9), with 'developer' and 'user' in 00 0.2; none of the four is in the vocabulary, and the one sentence that relates them is in ADR 0008 Context.
findings.scenario: A second adopter reads 'the maintainer's approval' in 05 5.3 and 'the operator decided' in 05 5.4 and concludes the product has two roles, one of which they must find or invent, and files an issue asking who the maintainer of their machine is.
findings.change: Add to 01 1.7 the rows operator (the person who runs romeu on a host, owns host settings and answers gates), maintainer (the person who merges and releases the product repository), developer or user (the operator as 00 0.2 counts them), and the sentence that today one person holds both roles; use each word only in its sense across the pages.
findings.cost: Three rows and a word-by-word pass.

findings.defect: The candidate machine has six states and the project record persists only awaiting, so five states live in process memory without the page saying which persist; the generation machine has no row for stop, pull, retire or salvage finding the sandbox absent, so by the page's own rule those cases exit 2 as illegal transitions.
findings.scenario: A sandbox dies; the operator runs romeu stop to be safe; the generation table has no row for stop on an absent sandbox; the command exits 2 with an illegal-transition id and a fix hint that names no verb, and the operator learns to use run, which creates a new sandbox they did not want.
findings.change: In 01 1.6 mark each state persisted or in-process, and add the rows for stop, pull, salvage (without --from-host) and retire when the sandbox is absent, or one sentence that every P command on an absent sandbox with an open generation preserves it the way run does.
findings.cost: A column and four rows, with the generated tests that follow.

findings.defect: The v3 descriptor grammar is parsed by internal/oci for images and by internal/render for local kits, 12 12.2 puts the grammar under oci only, no single owner is named, and nothing says what happens when sbx adds a capability type that the strict grammar refuses.
findings.scenario: sbx 0.50 adds a capability type to v3; every sync on every machine fails closed on the workload descriptor until a romeu release; the release teaches oci the type and forgets render; a personal kit that declares it still fails; the fix loosens the grammar in render 'for now' and I28's conformance holds for one parser.
findings.change: Name one package that owns the grammar and the normalized capability set, consumed by both oci and render; add a deferred row 'a capability type sbx adds after v1' with the trigger 'the first sync that fails on an unmodeled type', what holds (fail closed) and the cost (a release).
findings.cost: A decision on the package, a sentence in 1.4 and 6.1, one deferred row.

findings.defect: generations[] is an append-only array with a salvage[] array per element inside a file rewritten whole on every mutating command, with no bound, no compaction and no attic for closed generations.
findings.scenario: Three years of recreate on a busy project give a record of several hundred generations; every run rewrites it in full and status parses it on every call; S8 is measured against an empty record and nothing warns.
findings.change: Either move a closed generation to the state attic when its salvage refs are imported, keeping the open one and the last closed one in the record, or add a limits table (the style of 13 13.8) with a bound on generations in the record and a doctor warning past it.
findings.cost: One mechanism (a move on close) or one table and one doctor row.

findings.defect: Error ids are RJ-<exit><nn> with two digits per exit class, and the exit-2 class (eight meanings in one row) will exhaust first; no rule says whether an id may be reused or retired, and 04 never says what 13 13.7 implies: retiring an error id, a probe id or renaming a julieta command is a breaking change of the event format because ref and tool are valid by membership.
findings.scenario: A contributor renames julieta memory rm to memory remove for clarity; tools/new command scaffolds it, every check passes; after the release ingest rejects every spool file an older julieta wrote with the old name as event-domain, and the ledger has a year of rejected entries that cannot be told from attacks.
findings.change: In 04 4.1 say ids are never reused, widen nn to three digits or drop the exit prefix, and add the sentence 'an error id, a command name and a probe id are members of the ledger's tables (13 13.7): removing or renaming one is a breaking change of the event format'; have tools/new command print that sentence.
findings.cost: A decision on the id form, two sentences, one line in a scaffold.

findings.defect: sync does eleven jobs and julieta setup nine, and the cross-cutting side effects (which commands ingest, drain, snapshot, take the lock, run the preflight, append for idempotency) are hand lists in five sections that a new command must remember to join.
findings.scenario: A later PR adds romeu prune or julieta gc; its author does not know that ingest runs 'inside four commands' (13 13.4) or that the idempotency list of 04 4.1 is closed; the command skips ingest, events written before a sandbox removal are lost from the spool, and the meta-test passes because the list it reads is the same hand list.
findings.change: Add a 12 12.3 generator row: from the command definitions, a per-command table of side effects (preflight, lock, ingest, drain, snapshot, appending) rendered into 04 4.2 and 04 4.3 and read by the idempotency meta-test and by the test of T071; a command definition with no value for a side effect fails generation.
findings.cost: One generator row, a field per command definition, a table in 04 replacing five prose lists.

findings.defect: A per-subsystem error-id section exists for the ledger although it says the ledger has no catalog of its own; it is a second copy, by slug, of rows of the one table and a precedent for a 4.5.
findings.scenario: The memory store and salvage each gain an error section by imitation; the generated errors.md and the three hand sections disagree on exit codes within a year.
findings.change: Fold 4.4 into 13 13.4's rejection table (reason slugs only) and let docs/reference/errors.md be the one list; 04 keeps one sentence that subsystem reasons are rows of the table.
findings.cost: Words.

findings.defect: docs/spec/** is on no ask-first surface while the spec is the plan's source of truth and two checks read its Markdown tables as input (tools/ci vocabulary from 01 1.7; sequences from the index), so by 5.3's own logic ('the check code is the gate') gate inputs sit outside the gate, and a one-line ADR status change needs an approval while rewriting a security section does not.
findings.scenario: An agent PR edits the Not column of 01 1.7 to make its own wording pass tools/ci vocabulary and rewrites a residual-risk row of 05 5.4 in the same change; no approval line is required, the ruleset requires no review, and the change merges.
findings.change: Either move the check inputs out of prose (a vocabulary data file and a deferred-decisions data file under tools/ci, rendered into the spec) or add docs/spec.md and docs/spec/** to .github/ask-first.yaml as a 'specification' surface; state the choice in 05 5.3.
findings.cost: A decision on an ask-first surface (the operator's), one glob or two data files and two generator rows.

findings.defect: History has moved into the current-state spec: 05 5.4 carries dated measurements and 'replaces three rows round 4 recorded', 10 10.2's maintainer block is a dated procedure with a Try/Result table for tasks the plan has already ticked (T001 to T003), the index's status paragraph grows a clause per round, and deferred rows carry reasoning paragraphs; 12 12.5 says history lives in reviews and ADRs.
findings.scenario: In year three the index's status paragraph lists twelve rounds, 05 5.4's token row is a page, and a reader cannot find the current rule for a merge without reading what was measured on which day.
findings.change: Reduce each 5.4 row to risk, why accepted, mitigation and one link to the ADR or review that holds the measurement; move the maintainer block's items a to e and the Try/Result table to ADR 0008 or a docs note and keep in 10 10.2 the current ruleset requirements; make the index status one sentence and a link; add to sequences a bound on deferred-row cell length or the rule that reasoning goes to an ADR.
findings.cost: Words moved, one sequences clause.

findings.defect: Release signing exists only as a prohibition (the credential is outside GitHub, release.yml may not hold it, signing is an operator step) while S1's evidence says the attestation step 'signed them' and J1 verifies checksums and attestation only; no page says what is signed, with which tool, where the signature is published or how a user verifies it.
findings.scenario: v1.0.0 ships with checksums.txt and an attestation; the operator never signs anything because no step says to; three years on an incident asks whether any release was signed and the honest answer is that the spec forbade the wrong way and never described the right one.
findings.change: Decide and write it in 10 10.2 'Release and bootstrap': either 'v1 publishes no artifact signature beyond the provenance attestation' (and S1 and 05 5.4 say so, removing 'signed'), or the signed artifact, the tool, the publication location and the J1 verification command.
findings.cost: A decision on the release ask-first surface and a paragraph; possibly one J1 step.

findings.defect: Nine of the 36 deferred rows have triggers that only a person can notice ('the maintainer observes', 'the operator saying so', 'every 2 autonomous work sessions'), and the table names no reader and no cadence; ADR 0005 Consequences says 'A trigger nobody watches does not fire' and asks each row to name its check where one is possible, which no row does.
findings.scenario: The token-narrowing trigger of two sessions passes unnoticed because no tool counts sessions; doctor's ledger size warning fires on one machine and is read by nobody; both rows sit in the table for two years while the risk they guard is live.
findings.change: Add a fourth column 'Detected by': the doctor row, the ledger query, the tools/ci subcommand or 'review of this table at <event>'; replace the session-count trigger with an observable one (a count in the ledger, or a date is refused by rule 3 so make it 'the first run after a release'); sequences requires the column.
findings.cost: A column, 36 cells, one sequences clause; a small counter if the session trigger is kept.

findings.defect: A floor or pin bump needs probes re-run (10 10.3 'a new recording set') but result files docs/probes/<id>-<host>.json carry no sbx version, recordings are per version under e2e/testdata/sbx/<version>/, the lifecycle of 11 11.4 has no stale or superseded state, and no section says which bump re-runs which probe.
findings.scenario: The first sbx floor bump after v1 commits a second recording set; the block A results are overwritten or left naming the old version; tools/ci probes passes on results that never saw the new sbx; the A5 golden hashes stay recorded against a plan output sbx no longer accepts.
findings.change: Name results by id, host and sbx version (or one directory per version), add a 'stale' transition to 11 11.4 fired by a floor or pin change with the probe ids it stales, and add a 11.5 table: for each external pin of 12 12.1, the probes to re-run and the recordings to re-record.
findings.cost: A naming change, one lifecycle row, one table.

findings.defect: The product's architecture decisions (herdr as multiplexer, v3 kits, the secondary-repo clone, memory as plain files, stdlib flag over a CLI framework, GPL-3.0-only, the two gates) have no ADR, and 12 12.5 sends the docs module to five review-round files, which the index calls history, to write the initial set.
findings.scenario: A contributor proposes tmux in year two; the only written reasons for herdr are a dated paragraph in 06 6.4 and a review transcript; the discussion restarts from zero and the vocabulary of 'Why for us' asides is read as taste.
findings.change: Add to 12 12.5 a table of the decisions that need a record, each with the spec section that holds its current state, and have the docs module write from that table; the review rounds stay history.
findings.cost: One table of about ten rows; the ADRs themselves are plan work.

findings.defect: Four universal claims are refuted by the spec's own tables: 02 2.5 'julieta never guesses paths' beside four $HOME-derived paths no manifest field carries; 02 2.4 'the only environment override' beside tests that set HOME and XDG_*; 10 10.6 'every lifecycle is a transition table in internal/state' beside the probe lifecycle in tools/ci and an in-process candidate half; 04 4.1 'schema in schemas/' for every --json read command beside a schema list with none for status, doctor, ledger query, handoff or event list.
findings.scenario: A contributor trusts 'never guesses paths' and adds a fifth $HOME path without touching the manifest; another trusts 'schema in schemas/' and parses romeu status --json against a schema that does not exist.
findings.change: Make each claim true or weaker: list the four paths in the manifest or write 'derived from $HOME'; 'the only override of the settings path'; 'every lifecycle of host state'; add the missing schemas to 02 2.1 or drop the clause.
findings.cost: Words; possibly four manifest fields and five schemas.

findings.defect: The escape hatches (egress.tools, egress.extra, tool: other, --accept-loss, --overwrite-drift, retire --force) are each bounded but none is counted anywhere, so there is no way to see when one has become the main road.
findings.scenario: After a year every project carries egress.tools overrides because a catalog fix needs a release, most events say tool: other, and the catalog-gap signal the ledger exists for (13 13.9) is noise; nobody notices because no number says so.
findings.change: Add a doctor row that counts overrides per project and a ledger query that counts tool: other, and let status show --accept-loss and --overwrite-drift uses from the project record.
findings.cost: Two counts and a record field.

findings.defect: The publishing path is a deferral outside the deferred table: six rows of design including a host-settings key kits.source: published that 03 3.4 does not have, with the trigger 'when the product is promoted for public use (maintainer decision)', which ADR 0005 rule 3 would not accept as an event.
findings.scenario: A reader of 03 3.4 writes a settings validator; a reader of 06 6.6 writes kits.source into a settings file; the two never meet until a strict decoder refuses the key.
findings.change: Replace 6.6's table with one deferred row (what holds: local builds, trust is the release plus config commits; reopened by: the first user who is not the maintainer asks to consume a kit without a config repo clone, or the first kit signature sbx accepts) and move the six design rows to an ADR in Proposed status.
findings.cost: One deferred row, one ADR, a deletion.

findings.defect: Two long passages carry content the maintainer never needs to change the product: 00 0.6's 35-line critique of an external report with PDF page numbers, and 12 12.10's 150-line specification of a repository-metrics tool that 'gives a user's team nothing' and 'is a report and no merge gate'.
findings.scenario: The report publishes v2026.2 with new page numbers; DORA renames a metric; both pages are wrong and both are in the current-state spec of two CLIs.
findings.change: Move 0.6 to an ADR or a docs note cited from 0.2; keep in 12 12.10 the one paragraph that says the tool exists, measures this repository and gates nothing, and move the definitions and output format to a generated tools/ci reference page, with ADR 0004 as the decision.
findings.cost: Words moved; one generator row.

findings.defect: The module-boundary table lists packages in three rows and says nothing about a package in no row, so tools/ci imports is fail-open for every package added after v1 unless the code says otherwise; 02 2.1's '(romeu only)' comments are a second, unenforced copy.
findings.scenario: A PR adds internal/notify, imported by both binaries, which imports sbxdrv to read sandbox state; no row covers notify; imports passes; julieta now links the only code that runs sbx.
findings.change: Add to 10 10.7: 'a package under internal/ that no row names fails tools/ci imports', and drop the per-package comments from 02 2.1 in favour of a link to 10 10.7.
findings.cost: One sentence and the matching check behaviour.

findings.defect: ADR 0007 holds 300 lines of lint, directive and environment mechanism with pinned versions and function names (lintEnv, stepEnv, judgeCommit, resolveLintTools, allowedDirectives) in a record that is never rewritten, and already cites a plan deferred-decisions row ('whether agents push from a second account', reopened by block O1 item d) that no longer exists since ADR 0008 decided Q25; ADR 0001 holds the same kind of mechanism in its twenty rules.
findings.scenario: The first rename of lintEnv or bump of golangci-lint makes an accepted record wrong with no supersede; a reader who trusts ADRs over the spec implements the stale mechanism.
findings.change: Add to 12 12.5: a record holds the decision, the alternatives and the consequences; mechanism, versions and identifiers belong to the spec or the generated reference, which the record links; give ADR 0007 a Status line that its threat-model cross-reference is superseded by ADR 0008.
findings.cost: A rule in 12.5, one status line; a future trim of ADR 0007 and ADR 0001 by supersession.

findings.defect: Committed probe results pin spec heading anchors in affects (docs/spec/03-formats.md#32-project-spec-...), so a heading rename in the spec breaks or orphans committed data, and no rule says so.
findings.scenario: 03 3.2 is retitled when its table becomes a link to the reference (L3-1); the A10 result's affects anchor dangles; the resolvedBy check 'touches every affects path' still passes on the file, and the anchor is wrong forever.
findings.change: State in 12 12.5 that a heading cited by a committed probe result is renamed only with the result's affects updated in the same commit, and have tools/ci probes resolve each affects anchor like tools/ci docs resolves links.
findings.cost: A sentence and one check clause.

findings.defect: Three small gaps of explicitness in 03: a domain with no domains entry has two rules (treated as upload: true, and refused by CI) where one suffices; the manifest's 32 KiB cap has no stated behaviour at overflow; the lesson tag is a free-text tag that switches behaviour in three homes (3.9, 08 8.1, the skill).
findings.scenario: A large run layout with many repos exceeds 32 KiB and run fails in sbx with an error the spec never named; a second magic tag is added the same way as lesson and nobody can list the tags with behaviour.
findings.change: Keep one rule for the missing domains entry (the CI refusal), state the exit and id for a manifest over the cap, and list the tags with behaviour in 03 3.9 as a closed set.
findings.cost: Three sentences.

findings.defect: The package tree (02 2.1, about 27 packages), the module map (12 12.2, 24 ids) and S9's 90% list (8 packages) are three hand lists with different names for the same code (romeu-cli for internal/cli; memstore and ledger each covering two packages), and the plan found four paths no list owns.
findings.scenario: A package is renamed; the tree, the map and the coverage list each change in a different PR, and tools/ci coverage measures a package that no longer exists.
findings.change: Generate 02 2.1's tree and S9's list from the module map, or state in 12 12.2 that module ids name directories one to one and let a test hold the three lists equal.
findings.cost: One generator row or one test.

findings.defect: docs/acceptance.json is a one-shot v1.0.0 artifact that no later release reads, on the checks ask-first surface indefinitely, and nothing says how v1.1 states its criteria or when S1 to S11 are retired.
findings.scenario: v1.1 ships with S8's budget exceeded; the acceptance file still says pass for v1.0.0; nobody can say what v1.1 promised.
findings.change: Add to 10 10.5 the rule for later releases: the file is per release (docs/acceptance/<tag>.json) or retired after v1.0.0 with the criteria that stay living (S6, S8, S9) named as permanent tools/ci steps.
findings.cost: A decision and a paragraph.

findings.defect: 09 is the third copy of the command lines (with commands.yaml and the guides) and the only untied one, and it already disagrees with itself (the opening says J12 runs J1 steps 3 to 6, the J12 section says 1 to 5); J3 names a host multiplexer (cmux) that is a non-goal and no vocabulary term; J10 step 3 promises 'the hardened form' of an operator-typed git command that no page defines.
findings.scenario: The guide author follows the J12 section, the scenario author follows the opening, and the rule 13 check passes both because 09 is not what it reads.
findings.change: Make J12's two sentences agree; replace 'a cmux window' by 'a terminal window'; either define the hardened host form of git branch in 05 5.1 or have J10 recommend romeu pull and the review checkout instead of a host git command.
findings.cost: Words; one decision for J10.

findings.defect: ARCHITECTURE.md is the page the 'Simple and explicit' principle promises a newcomer, and nothing mechanical keeps it true: headings.yaml covers README.md and SECURITY.md only, its content is review, and only the diagrams are generated.
findings.scenario: After a hundred PRs the page describes the components of v1.0.0; the invariant list it carries misses I34 to I41; the newcomer the principle names reads it and builds against a model that is gone.
findings.change: Add ARCHITECTURE.md to headings.yaml, and a tools/ci docs rule that every invariant id of 05 5.2 and every module id of 12 12.2 appears in it, so a new id or module forces an edit.
findings.cost: One headings entry and one check clause.

findings.defect: The plan carries hand-kept derived facts that have already drifted: 'the seven decision records under adr/' (there are eight), counts such as '101 of 102 tasks', the traceability tables, and a second deferred-decisions table with the index's shape.
findings.scenario: Each count is wrong within three PRs and a reviewer reads the plan's numbers as facts about the spec.
findings.change: Generate the counts and traceability from the task fields or drop them; fold the plan's deferred rows into the index's table with a 'plan' marker so there is one table of one kind.
findings.cost: A small generator or a deletion.

postmortem: Written three years after v1.0.0 by the maintainer who inherited it; the product is used only by its first operator and has not merged a contributor's change in a year. 1. The spec became a museum and people stopped reading it: 03's tables were design input that the product generated elsewhere, 10 10.2 was 330 lines of check logic in English that the code had moved past, 05 5.2's Test cells named tests that had been renamed; contributors built against the spec, were refused by tools/ci, and learned to ignore the spec, then ARCHITECTURE.md, which nothing kept true (03, 05 5.2, 10 10.2, 12 12.1, 12 12.8, index Principles). 2. Every version bump was a documentation migration nobody made: mise, golangci-lint, revive, the runner labels, Go, testify, the sbx floor were each a number in prose; the first sbx floor bump needed block A re-run, the result files had no version in their names, the lifecycle had no stale state, and it took a quarter (10 10.2, 10 10.3, 11, ADR 0007). 3. State grew until it broke the time budget: projects/<name>.json held three hundred generations and was rewritten whole on every run; the ledger held two hundred thousand files and others.jsonl was rewritten for every project on every ingest; S8 was blown for a year because it had been measured on an empty ledger; doctor warned and nobody read doctor; rotation was designed in a hurry and broke 'nothing is ever deleted' (03 3.8, 13 13.5, 13 13.6, 13 13.8, index Deferred decisions). 4. The escape hatches became the road: egress.tools in every project because a catalog fix needed a release, tool: other in most events, --accept-loss in agents' habit after the first incomplete salvage, --overwrite-drift after every manual fix; nothing counted any of them (07 7.5, 13 13.2, 04 4.2, 01 1.6). 5. Ask-first was a record, not a control: one account, approval lines typed by the agent they gated, the operator reading the security log as the only check, a narrowing trigger of 'every 2 sessions' that nobody counted; in year two a prompt injection in a dependency's README reached three other repositories through the operator's token; the spec had said all of this honestly in four places, and honesty is not a mechanism (05 5.4, 12 12.4, ADR 0008, index Deferred decisions). 6. Cross-cutting chores leaked: ingest lived inside four commands by a hand list in three places, the drain inside julieta setup, sync did eleven jobs and setup nine; a new command skipped ingest, another broke idempotency, and the meta-tests read the same hand lists (04 4.1, 04 4.2, 04 4.3, 13 13.3, 13 13.4). 7. The deferred-decisions table was where decisions went to die: thirty-six rows at v1, eighty by year two, nobody owned reading it, triggers fired silently as ADR 0005 had warned, and features landed without rows because the table was too long to check; the same facts lived in 05 5.4 and two ADRs and drifted (index, ADR 0005, 05 5.4). 8. The why of the architecture was in review transcripts: the eight ADRs covered process; herdr, v3 kits, the secondary clone, memory as files, stdlib flag and the gates had no record; T096 to T100 mined six review rounds into forty thin ADRs without alternatives; the first contributor who wanted tmux re-litigated everything and won by attrition (12 12.5, 06 6.4, 02 2.6, 08 8.1). 9. The two descriptor parsers diverged when sbx added a capability type: oci learned it, render did not, personal kits failed sync for a release, and the fix made the grammar lenient for now (01 1.4, 06 6.1, I28). 10. The error-id space and the ledger's membership tables froze the CLI: renaming a command or retiring an id was a ledger major, so nobody did either, and exit-2 ids reached RJ-299 (04 4.1, 13 13.2, 13 13.7). What I would not normally say: the spec was written for its reviewers, not for me; it argues, dates, cites and defends across nine thousand lines for two command-line tools, and the volume was itself the failure, because agents copied that density into code comments and PR bodies until nothing was readable. The one-person premise (one maintainer, one account, one machine, the name is the identity) was baked into identity and storage rather than isolated, so when a second person arrived nothing fit. And the page that kept the product alive as long as it did was 13, the one that said for every guarantee whether a mechanism or a promise stood behind it; had every page been written like 13 this postmortem would not exist.
lens_critique: This lens prices stability above learning speed and treats every duplicated fact as a defect, which is right for a product in its third year and partly wrong for a v1 written before any code by one maintainer with agents: some duplication is the cost of a spec that is a design input meant to be replaced by generated reference, and 13 shows the authors know how to write the mechanism-versus-promise split when they choose to. The lens also assumes a human inherits; here agents inherit, and agents read tools/ci output and generated reference rather than prose, so prose staleness hurts less than this lens weighs it. Finally, the three-year horizon may be the wrong success test for a product whose premises (one developer, a v3 kit milestone, one agent's hook names) may not survive eighteen months: the better definition of success might be cheap to throw away and rebuild from the generated truth, not cheap to maintain, and this lens would then over-invest in single sources for things that should simply be deleted.
missing_viewpoint: The first-time contributor, human or agent, writing pull request number thirty against CONTRIBUTING.md, tools/new and the generated reference: every lens in the set is a user, a guardian or a maintainer, and nobody is the person to whom the index's promise 'inviting to contributors: a newcomer reads ARCHITECTURE.md, runs one command to scaffold what they add' is made.
